extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature (scientists, students, and prospective applicants for academic posts, scholarships, and technical courses)
extracted.subtask_description: Announcements of academic posts, scholarships, courses and their eligibility/selection/application rules (deadlines, required documents, qualifications, and disqualifying practices). Mostly UK institutions and some colonial posts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Johnston Chemical Scholarship — eligibility and award basis
rubrics_metrics.description: This Scholarship (£60), tenable for one year, together with a prize in books to the value of £5, will be awarded on the result of an Examination in Chemistry, together with Crystallography or Mineralogy, to be held during the week commencing September 30, 1907.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates must be Bachelors in Science of a British University of not more than three years' standing; names to be sent in on or before September 31 to the undersigned (F. H. Pruen, Secretary).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarships and Exhibitions awarded on year's work
rubrics_metrics.description: A considerable number of Scholarships and Exhibitions are open for competition at the beginning of each Session, and several are awarded at the end of each Session on the result of the year's work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection for some awards is explicitly based on academic performance across the academic session rather than a single examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum academic qualification for certain appointments
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should possess an Honours Degree in Chemistry and should have worked in a good laboratory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specified as a requirement for the London County Council Lecturer on Chemistry (Paddington Technical Institute). Additional desirable attributes (see separate entry) may be listed but the Honours degree and laboratory experience are minimum stated qualifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desirable experience: technical work and class teaching
rubrics_metrics.description: Experience in technical work and class teaching desirable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as desirable (not strictly essential) for posts such as the L.C.C. Lecturer on Chemistry — likely used as tie-breaker / merit factor in appointment decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role-specific competence (chief assistant / laboratory head)
rubrics_metrics.description: Engineer, competent to take charge of the Engineering Laboratory, and to lecture on Mechanical Engineering and Applied Mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appointments requiring both practical supervisory ability (take charge of laboratory) and lecturing competence; competence to manage laboratory operations and teach relevant subjects is an explicit selection criterion (City and Guilds of London Institute post).

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching-post subject competence and essential experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates will be required to teach Physics, Chemistry, and Elementary Mathematics; successful teaching experience essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated requirement for the Science and Mathematical Master at Auckland Technical College — emphasizes both subject-matter competence and demonstrable teaching experience as selection criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application format and supporting documents requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications should be made on the official form, to be obtained with particulars of the appointment; applications must be accompanied by copies (not originals) of three recent testimonials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple institution notices repeat this procedural requirement. Deadlines and the address/office to which forms must be returned are specified in each advertisement; applicants are expected to follow the official form and attach testimonials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postal application procedural detail (stamped addressed envelope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates applying through the post should enclose a stamped and addressed envelope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific administrative request from the London County Council listing; intended to facilitate correspondence by return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canvassing disqualifies applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Canvassing, either directly or indirectly, will be held to be a disqualification for employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit anti-canvassing rule in the L.C.C. advertisement — a mandatory disqualifier rather than a desirability criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline compliance for applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must be returned not later than [specified date] and will be considered only if received by that time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each post/scholarship specifies a return-by date (e.g., applications to reach by a.m. on Saturday, September 28; forms to be received not later than October 3). Timely submission is a precondition for consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection for scholarships open only to degree-holders within specified standing
rubrics_metrics.description: Some scholarships are open only to candidates who hold a Degree (or equivalent) and meet additional standing conditions (e.g., not more than three years' standing after B.Sc.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility windows (years since degree) and degree-type requirements are used to limit the candidate pool for certain awards (example: Johnston Chemical Scholarship).

rubrics_metrics.name: Open admissions / non-discrimination (classes open to both sexes)
rubrics_metrics.description: All classes are open to both sexes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated policy for certain colleges (e.g., City of London College) indicating gender-inclusive eligibility for courses; this is an explicit institutional standard affecting admissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection by competitive examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards and scholarships may be awarded 'on the result of an Examination' held at specified times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several notices indicate that competition outcomes are determined by formal examinations (e.g., Johnston Scholarship) — the examination content and scheduling form part of the selection rubric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection by results of internal year performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain Scholarships and Exhibitions are awarded on the result of the year's work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions may use cumulative internal assessment across the academic year (coursework/results) as the basis for awarding some scholarships/exhibitions rather than a single external exam.
